newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania wheat withstands wet weather - official.
newsitem.headline: Romania wheat withstands wet weather - official.

text.p: Romania will have a good quality wheat crop this year, despite the recent adverse weather, and this year's exports will not be affected, a senior Romanian official said on Monday.

"There is no reason to believe that the quality of the wheat crop has diminished following last week's meteorological conditions," Trita Fanita, chairman of the Senate's commission for agriculture, forestry and food, said in a statement.

The statement followed remarks made last week by Vasile Duta, head of the National Agency for Agricultural Products, who said rains over the past week had affected the quality of Romania's milling wheat and that exports could be below the planned 2.4 million tonnes.
The Agriculture Ministry expects a bumper wheat crop of 7.07 million tonnes in 1997, almost double the level last year.
Romania and other east European countries were hit by bad weather last week.
But Fanita, who is also the general manager of the local Agroexport SA, a major grain trading company, said the wet weather made no impact on Romania's wheat crop.
"This year, the good wheat crop has a quality which makes it fit for milling. Consequently it will be sought for export," Fanita said.
On Monday an analyst at the institute for agricultural research in Fundulea, near Bucharest, said that only part of the wheat harvested so far had been hit by bad weather.
"I wouldn't say that the majority of the wheat crop has been affected, from the quality point of view," he added.
He said wheat harvested in the western counties of Banat and Oradea showed the beginnings of germination.
"This affects to a certain extent the quality of the wheat harvested in that area," the analyst said.
The Fundulea institute had not received similar reports on wheat harvested in southern regions, traditionally the country's main grain supplier, he said.
"It is true that it rained there every day, but luckily it was for short periods of time, and such a process (germination) has not started," the analyst said.
